text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.6% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of nearly 10% that began right after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has lost about $18 per share since late October, tracking alongside a broader pullback in oil prices—US crude is now trading around $99.60 a barrel, down from levels that would have been higher when the stock peaked. While the company was highlighted as a stock to watch in mid-November coverage, the earnings announcement appears to have triggered selling rather than buying interest.

The broader context cutting against energy stocks right now is political. A Democratic sweep in midterm elections has renewed focus on renewable energy policy and reduced the likelihood of Trump-era opposition to clean energy investments—a headwind for traditional oil and gas companies as the sector rotates. Meanwhile, despite ongoing Iran tensions that historically support oil prices, the geopolitical risk premium appears insufficient to offset investor concerns about longer-term energy transition trends.
